name: RecordDetailShell
intent: Left section rail beside a single scrolling content column, for a record whose detail genuinely warrants navigation.
when: A record has five or more substantial sections
One section at a time is the right reading unit
A section owns the page height itself, such as a graph canvas — pass flush
whenNot: The record has a few short sections -> stack them full-width with no rail
Navigating between records rather than within one -> use SideMenu directly
The app shell's own sidebar -> use CoreAppSidebar

chooseOver.component: SideMenu plus a hand-built content column
chooseOver.because: The shell owns the md-breakpoint column flip, the min-h-0 chain that keeps the column scrolling instead of the page, and the unpadded scroll owner wrapping a padded well — three details four detail pages each re-derived and one of which is easy to get subtly wrong.

title.note: The record's TYPE, not its name — "Object type", "Process".

sections.note: Grouped section entries; ids address them.

flush.note: Place children as a direct flex child, for a section that owns the page height.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Section ids must be unique across all groups.

states.default: Rail on the left from md up, one section rendered in a padded scrolling column.
states.narrow: Below md the rail becomes a horizontal row above the content.
states.flush: The section is a direct flex child and owns its own padding, overflow and min-h-0 chain.

allowedPlacement: a record detail page below its header
forbiddenPlacement: a record with only a few short sections
evaluationCriteria: The content column scrolls, not the page.
A record with few short sections does not use this at all.

lineage.authoredBy: Extracted from the four SideMenu detail pages found in the missing-widgets template review (2026-08-25)

extracted: unpadded scroll owner around a padded content well

lineage.supersedes: The inline SideMenu rows in wc3-object-type-detail, wc3-action-type-detail, wc3-process-detail and wc3-product-detail
notes: Scoped on purpose: the interface, pipeline and shared-property detail pages stack full-width and must NOT adopt this.
flush exists for wc3-process-detail's canvas section, which owns the page height.

usage: Use RecordDetailShell to enhance your user interface. This component provides a consistent, accessible, and well-designed solution for this use case.
RecordDetailShell integrates seamlessly with other components in the design system. Follow the established patterns and guidelines to ensure consistency across your application.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the section rail — the record's TYPE, not its name. "Object type", "Process".

props.name: sections
props.description: The sections, grouped. Ids are what `activeSectionId` and `onSectionChange` speak in.

props.name: flush
props.description: Render the content as a direct flex child instead of inside the padded, scrolling well — for a section that owns the page height itself, such as a full-bleed graph canvas. When this is set the section must manage its own padding, overflow and `min-h-0` chain.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Extra classes on the padded content well. Ignored when `flush`.

anatomy.description: RecordDetailShell is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
